career.role: Team Leader, Africa Justice and Peacebuilding Working Group (AJPWG)
career.scope: As part of Catholic Relief Services, the AJPWG included five technical advisors supporting CRS' regional offices and country programs in Africa concerning peace, conflict, social cohesion and good governance. In this capacity, hosted and mentored four Mandela Washington Fellows in their Professional Development Experiences.

career.role: Chief of Party, REGAL-IR: Resilience and Economic Growth in Arid Lands – Improving Resilience in Kenya
career.scope: Managed a $45.5m five-year resilience strengthening project in northern Kenya, funded by USAID/Kenya with support from the Bureau of Food Security and Feed the Future in Washington, DC. The project aimed to raise living standards, improve community well-being, and increase food security for drought-affected and impoverished pastoralists in northern Kenya.

career.role: Chief of Party, EWARDS: Early Warning and Response Design Support
career.scope: Managed all facets of a $4.5m two-and-a-half-year conflict early warning and response project in West Africa, contracted under USAID/West Africa with technical support from the Office for Conflict Management and Mitigation (CMM).

Provided technical leadership for ARD's institutional development and governance sector; led ARD's Civil Society Strengthening Practice Area; contributed specialized short- and long-term expertise for task orders and projects on demand; ensured client satisfaction in review, analysis, planning, training and implementation of projects; managed and provided guidance to ARD staff and consortium partners on USAID's Building Recovery and Reform through Democratic Governance (BRDG) IQC.

career.role: Civil Society Analyst and Social Scientist
career.scope: Provided technical assistance on behalf of USAID's Bureau for Africa, Office of Sustainable Development (AFR/SD), and Bureau for Democracy, Conflict and Humanitarian Assistance, Office of Democracy and Governance (DCHA/DG). Assisted USAID missions and US embassies in democracy and governance (DG) and civil society programming, including strategic planning, design, implementation, performance monitoring and evaluation; mentored field officers and implementing partners through TDYs, field assessments and backstopping; co-led efforts to integrate governance and other sectors, including food security and HIV/AIDS. As Cognizant Technical Officer (CTO), managed the African Leadership Program with the Les Aspin Center for Government at Marquette University; the Africa Liaison Program Initiative (ALPI) with InterAction; the Global Civil Society Strengthening Cooperative Agreement with AED; the Civil Society Sustainability Study with MSI; and the NGO Law Reform activity with ICNL. Was CTO for the Africa Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) activity implemented by the Foundation for Democracy in Africa (FDA).

Provided technical assistance in private and public funding, program planning and proposal writing to community-based groups working to prevent alcohol, tobacco and other drug (ATOD) abuse among youth in local communities across Indiana.

career.role: Guinea Project Assistant and Deputy Chief of Party
career.scope: Provided technical assistance to the Ministry of Agriculture and Animal Resources (MARA) to manage its physical inventory. career.scope: Organized and operated emergency feeding programs and grain distributions, and designed and conducted nutritional surveys in the Mayo-Kebbi and Chari-Baguirmi regions of Chad; hired, trained and supervised 25 local staff; coordinated with local officials and maintained operational liaison with partners.

Co-managed a 60-seat facility with indoor-outdoor dining and nightly entertainment for a popular restaurant in Puerto Princesa City. Supervised and trained a local staff of 15, managed inventory, hired bands and entertainers, handled financial reports, and tended bar.

Coordinated, monitored and reported on the implementation of protection and resettlement services within the Vietnamese Refugee Center (VRC); planned projects and budgets for the VRC; directed housing and maintenance projects; oversaw sanitation and food supply; maintained productive relationships with Philippine military and local government officials on behalf of UNHCR; coordinated international field staff of eight; liaised with 15 to 20 voluntary agencies operating inside the camp.

Taught English as a foreign language (TEFL) and geography (in French) to high school students in Bas-Zaire; served as Faculty Advisor for the school's animal husbandry projects in pisciculture and rabbit-raising; trained incoming Peace Corps volunteers in TEFL for the Centre de Formation of the University of Zaire, Bukavu.

career.organization: Michigan Economics for Human Development / Catholic Human Development Office
career.scope: Directed and implemented programs in emergency assistance, relocations, job placement and adult basic education for an NGO assisting migrant and seasonal farmworkers in southwestern Michigan; managed two offices; supervised 11 field office staff; helped establish an area migrant services advisory council.

consulting.role: Team Leader, mid-term evaluation of the Civil Society Media Leadership (CSML) program
consulting.scope: Evaluation conducted under The Mitchell Group's Liberia Monitoring and Evaluation Program (L-MEP) of a program implemented by IREX. Led a four-person team in a formative evaluation of a five-year $11.9m project that aimed to increase the capacity of civil society and community radio to inform and engage citizens and to encourage active participation in civic matters, policy and politics across seven counties of Liberia. The team made three presentations to stakeholders and produced a 30-page evaluation report. The evaluation combined a document and M&E data review with key informant interviews, focus groups, a radio call-in program, and on-site observations in Monrovia and across four counties.

consulting.organization: Catholic Relief Services, for the US State Department
consulting.role: Team Leader, final evaluation of “Protecting Communities from Violence Through Improved Communications”
consulting.scope: Funded by the US State Department's Bureau for Population, Refugees, and Migration (BPRM). Led a two-person team to evaluate a 22-month, $1.7m community protection project in eastern DRC. The project's goal was to develop local capacity for enhanced security and protection from armed attacks by organizing 40 community protection committees in South Kivu and Orientale provinces and equipping them with HF radios to communicate with UN (MONUSCO) field bases and with Caritas partners in four dioceses of eastern DRC. The team made two presentations and produced a 30-page report. The evaluation combined desk study, document review, key informant interviews, on-site observations in South Kivu, and a review of the project's M&E data.

Produced a winning 25-page technical proposal responding to a USAID/Kenya solicitation for “Resilience and Economic Growth in the Arid Lands – Improving Resilience Project in Kenya (REGAL-IR),” a five-year $45m award. Assisted Adeso and seven sub-partners to develop an integrated, cross-sector approach to strengthening resilience in five northern counties of Kenya. Advised on staffing and program design.

Produced a winning 30-page technical proposal responding to a USAID/West Africa solicitation for “Evaluation and Analytical Services for the Regional Peace and Governance Programs,” worth $8.2m over five years. Handled the full spectrum of proposal preparation: coordinated a partnership between TMG and the University of Pittsburgh, designed the staffing matrix, drafted and finalized the technical approach, supervised the M&E sections, recruited short-term technical assistance for the consultant roster, identified and recruited five West African NGO partners, and designed and administered a partner technical capacity building questionnaire.

consulting.organization: University of Pittsburgh, Graduate School of Public and International Affairs (GSPIA), The Governance Group
consulting.scope: Produced the Governance Group's technical concept note responding to a solicitation from the USAID Higher Education Solutions Network. The purpose of the solicitation was to find new approaches to solving major development challenges by creating and leveraging virtual networks of experts affiliated with universities and research institutions.

consulting.scope: Conducted field research in West Africa and produced WANEP's technical proposal in response to USAID/DCHA/CMM's FY12 Annual Program Statement on people-to-people conflict management, “Conflict Mitigation and Reconciliation Programs and Activities.” The proposal supported USAID's aims to assist the people of Côte d'Ivoire to further national reconciliation following a decade of civil war, political partitioning of the country, and the presidential succession crisis of 2011–2012.

Conducted desk research, provided input to interview instruments, consulted with project stakeholders and CRS staff in Burundi, and drafted and finalized the technical content of the proposal.

Researched and developed the annual statistics questionnaire for the Ministry of Education and Professional Training (MEPU-FP) in Guinea.
